reran: cmd.sh on w3-int reproduces actual.txt exactly (9 FAIL lines for ArrayDeque and UnrolledBuffer, two of them OutOfMemoryError under -Xmx300m; ArrayBuffer and ListBuffer throw ConcurrentModificationException). w3-base and the 2.13.18 library jar print the same 13 lines.
user_impact: As GC7, for buffers: d.addAll(d.view.reverse), q.patchInPlace(i, q.view.map(f), n), buf --= buf.view.slice(a, b) on ArrayDeque, Queue, Stack or UnrolledBuffer. Rare in practice; Queue and Stack are the classes most likely to meet it.
fixability: clear cut for these two classes once the snapshot-or-reject question of scala/bug#12121 is settled the way #534, #538 and #548 already assume (snapshot): read a source that might be a proxy before the first write in ArrayDeque.addAll, IndexedBuffer.patchInPlace, Shrinkable.subtractAll for buffers, and in UnrolledBuffer for any non-strict source. One extra copy for lazy arguments; no binary cost.
links: GC7 (primary; its matrix has these cells). LM2 (#548), LM3 (#538), LB5 (#534): the fixes these cells escape. scala/bug#12121.
note: Real, but the same root cause and the same upstream ticket as GC7, and GC7's matrix lists every cell here, so keep GC7 and fold this in; what this one adds is the non-terminating UnrolledBuffer.addAll(self.iterator) reproduction. The right outcome is a wider fix on #548 and #538 rather than new pull requests per cell. What the earlier drafts cover: retronym/scala#534 makes ArrayBuffer.insertAll/prependAll copy a possible proxy before shifting (addAll of a view still throws ConcurrentModificationException, which is fail-fast and not counted). #548 does the same for ArrayDeque.insertAll and for patchInPlace at index 0; it leaves ArrayDeque.addAll (own override that appends while reading; wrong for a reversed view), IndexedBuffer.patchInPlace with from > 0 and replaced > 0 (the PR text says so; 8 wrong cells each for ArrayDeque, Queue, Stack), and subtractAll (Shrinkable's default; IndexOutOfBoundsException or wrong). #538 clones only when the source is the UnrolledBuffer itself (eq), so every view or iterator of it is still wrong in insertAll, prependAll, patchInPlace and subtractAll and addAll does not terminate. #535 is tests only (label no-fix) for addAll on HashSet, LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, LinkedHashMap, TreeMap; it changes no behaviour, and does not mention HashMap, CollisionProofHashMap, LongMap, AnyRefMap, the java.util wrappers, or subtractAll on any set or map. The three ConcurrentModificationException lines (ArrayBuffer.addAll of a view, ListBuffer.subtractAll) are printed as FAIL but are fail-fast behaviour, which the brief says is not a finding; the detail says so, the output does not.
